question.text: If the last business day of June is 30th (Monday), what is the expiry date for the June monthly USDINR futures contract, assuming there are no trading holidays other than Saturday and Sunday?

explanation.text: The Logic: Pages 50 and 56 of the NISM Series I Currency Derivatives workbook (December 2025) state that a monthly currency futures contract expires two working days prior to the last business day of the expiry month, at 12:30 pm. With 30th June (Monday) as the last business day and no trading holidays other than Saturday and Sunday, counting back two working days gives 27th June (Friday) and then 26th June (Thursday) as the expiry date. The Trap: Working days exclude weekends, so 28th June (Saturday) cannot be the expiry; 27th June (Friday) is only one working day prior to the last business day; and 30th June (Monday) is the last business day itself. Note: The "no holidays apart from Saturday and Sunday" assumption is added to the stem because the workbook example on pages 50 and 56 explicitly relies on that assumption.
